title: An integer literal passed where a `?uint` is declared carries the `int` tag.
text: `rule:types/arithmetic` makes a literal take the integer type its position declares. At a `?uint` parameter the position is tagged, and the literal is lowered as an `int` and tagged as one. So `class Shop { public static function take(?uint $limit): string { return $limit is uint ? "uint" : "not uint"; } } echo Shop::take(1);` prints `not uint`. The checked build stops at the parameter (`NOVIS_CHECK_TYPES=1`, the `spreadsheet-*` reader cases, through `Reader::with`'s `$limit`). Closing it lowers the literal at the union's integer member when the union has `uint` and not `int`, with a conformance case for the parameter, a property and a return.
